utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't think the registrar said anything different to what she's said every day, so you can just copy out what she usually says. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to the second group that you described yesterday, you mentioned that you did not watch again so closely as during the first incident. Did you see all these people that you have mentioned to us lining or only some of them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw all the men who were lined up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had started to describe to us the third incident, and you had mentioned that Vahida Dzemal was involved in this and you have already told us who he was. And then you mentioned that Fuad Mandzo was also in the third group. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fuad Mandzo was a medical technician and he worked in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how old he was? Was he a young man, an old man?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was barely 25, if.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know him from before, from before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did, but none too well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he lived before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He lived in the village of Mijakovici, not far from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also mentioned already Enes Uzunovic being in this third group. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Enes Uzunovic was also a medical technician and he worked in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned Nermin Hadzimusic. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hadzimusic had his coffee shop and lived at Brod.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we had already mentioned yesterday that Vahida Dzemal was C-27, Mandzo Fuad C-16, and Enes Uzunovic C-26. This Nermin Hadzimusic is not on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned yesterday Adil Krajcin. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adil Krajcin was one of the commercial directors in the brown coal mine in Miljevina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is person C-14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also mentioned Altoka. Is this one person or several persons?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two persons, actually, Alija and Miralem Altoka, the same last name, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they both in the same group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both were in the same group.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the person Alija Altoka is C-1, and Miralem Altoka is not on schedule C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned a person Ismet Karahasanovic. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ismet Karahasanovic was taken away from the fourth group. Karahasanovic was a forwarder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also mentioned a person Islambasic, Suad. Was he in this third group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Islambasic, Suad was in the fourth group. He was a car mechanic and he had a job at the Ozren company at Brod.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour the last two mentioned persons are not on Schedule C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall anyone else when was in this third group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember Cedic, Enko; Pasalic, Adnan; and Granov, Adil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Enko Cedic, who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know Enko Cedic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How then do you know the name? How could you recognise that he was in this group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other people recognised him and they told me about it. They knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you about it while you were in the KP Dom, while this actually was happening, or later on?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, while I was at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Enko Cedic, that's C-5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned Adnan Pasalic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pasalic, Adnan is from Godijen and he completed a secondary vocational school, technical school.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This person is not on the -- on Schedule C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned Granov, Adil. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adil Granov was an engineer specialising in PTT communications. He was employed at the post office in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is C-9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned yesterday that Abdurahman Cankusic was also taken away. Was he in the third group or the fourth group, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the third group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a car mechanic employed in Hidrogradnja, Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was -- is he a brother of Refik?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the brother of Refik Cankusic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the person C-3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the father was -- the father of the Cankusic brothers was actually also aware of what was happening. What became of the father? Did he survive the camp?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The father was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you meet him later on?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he is alive or is he missing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. Right now, I don't know whether he's alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you see -- is there anyone else in this group or was it those you just mentioned? Do you recall anyone else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not from that group, I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see -- what did you see happen to this group of people? What did you actually see yourself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the same procedure. They were taken into the KP Dom, one by one. After that, the procedure was the same: beatings, screams. However, that took place in the other rooms and you could only hear the sound. You could only hear the moans and cries of the people who were being beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "the other rooms," from -- could you locate from where the sounds came from, from which part of the administration building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the central part of the administration building, from the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "central part," what is for you the central part in relation to the entrance door? To the left or the right or around the entrance door? What would it be?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look straight ahead from my dormitory, it is to the left-hand side of the entrance door, the building that was facing the canteen from the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, if we are going to have troubles - and obviously the witness does have troubles on this, these questions of geography - should we have the plan turned upside down for him?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Because I think that it may be important. It's a little bit difficult even for me, with a plan in front of me now, to work out where he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. With the help of the usher, would the witness please be shown the Exhibit 6/1? I have it here. And please put it upside down, so this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, would you please have a look at it, and point to us from where you could hear the sounds? Maybe you could first show us the entrance door so that we know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Could we start with his dormitory?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please show us your dormitory first, where you were, where you were. Were you --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at the - well, I have it the wrong way around - at the buildings Zgrada BR 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, were you still in Room 11 when that happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was in Room 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the Room 11? It was above the magazine?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the windows by the wall could have been by the warehouse. The other dormitory, I'm sorry, not mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you now point to us the entrance door to the administration building?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He's pointing at where the door is. I think we can agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did the sounds come from? Could you point the direction?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These parts here, these parts of the building, from the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at the two rooms called Soba 1 and Soba 2. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the -- how long did you hear the sounds of beatings, from this other part of the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people were taken out around 6.00 and 7.00, and then it went on until late at night. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything else after the beating -- the sounds of beating had stopped?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same procedure like for the previous two groups: One bullet was fired per person, and then, of course, shaking off the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any of these people you just listed again, or did you hear of them again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw them, nor did I hear anything about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have contacts with any of the relatives of these detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from those groups I only had contacts with the family of Adil Granov.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did -- to whom did you speak from this family and what did you learn from them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mother, the wife, and the sister. And I found out that they did not know anything about him either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was another group of detainees taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from this fourth group that you mentioned, the following persons were also taken out: Paco Ismet, Sofradzija Mehmed, Dzano Hasan, Dzendusic Ramo. I think that that's it. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Dzelil Alija also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you, in relation to the third group, I forgot to ask you: Who of these people were in your room, Room 11, at that time when they were taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Islambasic Suad was in my dormitory out of the third group, also Karahasanovic Ismet, Granov Adil. Because practically, after he disappeared, I remained in his bed. I don't think there was anyone else from my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have mentioned Paco Ismet. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paco Ismet is a mechanical engineer -- was a mechanical engineer and was one of the directors in Focatrans.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is not on Schedule C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in your room when he was taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he was not in my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned Sofradzija Mehmed. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sofradzija Mehmed was a legal officer at the Municipal Assembly of Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this person have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mesa.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is mentioned not on Schedule C but on Schedule B-52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned Dzendusic Ramo. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzendusic Ramo worked in the secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in your room, in Room 11, when he was taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he was not in my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Sofradzija Mehmed, was he in your room when he was taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sofradzija Mehmed was in Room 22. He was detained by himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I saw him at the window of that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ismet Paco, was he in Room 11?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not Room 11. As far as Ismet Paco is concerned, I really don't know what room he was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a person Dzelil Alija. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzelil Alija was an economist. He worked in the Perucica Trading Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is not on Schedule C. Sorry. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned a Hasan Dzano. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Dzano Hasan is concerned, the only thing I know is that he was from the village of Josanica and that he was a farmer.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is not on Schedule C but under B-18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know a Cedik [phoen] Zaim?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's something wrong with the sound. Do you mean Zaim Cedic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zaim Cedic, yes, I know him well. Zaim Cedic had a degree in law. He worked in the Sutjeska-Tjentiste National Park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he also taken in any of these groups?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He was in that fourth group.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is not on Schedule C but on B-11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know a Rasim Kajgana?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Rasim Kajgana. Rasim Kajgana was the manager of a shop in UPI.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he taken away in any of the groups? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was taken out in the fourth group.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is mentioned under B-32.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what did you see in relation to the fourth group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure was the same like with the previous group. They were taken in one by one; the same cries, the same moans, the same sounds from the rooms I mentioned a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which rooms? You mean the room that you could look into or the room that you mentioned was in the centre of the administration?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rooms that were in the central part of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see all of them lining in front of the entrance or only some?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I certainly saw all of those who were lining up in front of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of them return, or did you hear of them or meet them later on?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single one of them has returned, nor do I know of their fate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you later on meet relatives of any of these people that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I had contact with the wife of Mehmed Sofradzija; with a daughter and two sons of Ramo Dzendusic; with Ismet Karahasanovic's brother; with the mother of Suad Islambasic; with the father of Zaim Cedic; and I don't think that I had contact with others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you learn from the relatives that you just mentioned? What did they tell you or ask you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me absolutely whether I knew what happened to these people. I did not tell any of these people about anything that I had not seen myself. I told them that I just know that they were taken out and I know nothing else, and they replied to me that they didn't know anything either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the previous statements that you gave to the Prosecutor's Office, that is to the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, you also mentioned a person Kemo Dzelilovic. What can you -- do you know of such a person?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know Kemo Dzelilovic very well. He was a teacher at the Foca high school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him when we came to get meals and when we were leaving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also taken out among the others who I mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall in which group he was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the first group.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this person is mentioned under C-7 and also B-19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your previous statement, you also mentioned a Juso Dzamalja. Who was he and what did you see happen to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Juso Dzamalja was a retiree. I saw him as he came for meals and left. As far as I know, Juso Dzamalja hanged himself in the premises of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being taken for beatings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your previous statement, you also mentioned a person Omer Mujezinovic. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Omer Mujezinovic is from Ustikolina. I knew him because he was not a normal person. Let me put it very simply: He was crazy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see him in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in your room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not in my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few persons similar to Omer. There was Hakan Hajdarevic, then Bunda and Culum. All of these men had mental problems. One day, they called out their names and they took them in a direction unknown to myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour this person Omer Mujezinovic is mentioned under C-18 and B-42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you also mentioned a person Ismet Deleut. I don't know if I pronounced it properly.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he, and what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ismet Deleut, I know that he was a farmer from the village of Mazetici. I also know that he was taken to the isolation cell once and never returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this pattern of beatings, how did this affect you personally?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely unpleasant. To begin with, those screams and those blows, so the fierceness, the noise. I was all shaken. At times, I tied my ears with a towel or whatever rag I could find just not -- just so as not to listen to it all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see detainees being beaten in the canteen or in the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it in front of the canteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was beaten by whom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we would finish the lunch, we would line up in front of the canteen and there was a guard, Predrag Stefanovic with us, from the canteen one of the last ones or perhaps the last one, Nihad Pasovic, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. called Pace, came out of the canteen, and the above-mentioned guard approached him and simply started to beat him, first kicking him in the ankle, then slap him in the face and use his fists against him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why this guard beat Pace?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I never knew that and I don't know it today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it happened in August. Which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the incident 5.10 in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see detainees being beaten in the yard by soldiers or policemen? I mean outsiders, not staff on KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened sometime around the 31st of October, 1992, when a group of inmates was to be exchanged and go to Konjic. We -- no, sorry, Room 18 was having lunch at the time. It was around 1.00, perhaps 1.20. And then five soldiers wearing cowboy clothes walked in, of course, with their rifles on their shoulders, and two more of them stayed in the door, behind the door. And they approached the inmates column and all five of them began to beat whoever they could lay their hands on. And it went on for about half an hour, and then they ordered everybody to lie down on the ground. Mitar Rasevic naturally watched it all from the window. And about 15 minutes later, he turned up in the KP Dom's yard, stood some ten or 20 metres away from the column, and watched it in silence. And the guards who guarded us, who saw us go to the canteen and back from the canteen, they also just watched it in silence. Nobody did anything. But it so happened when they stopped all this beating, they walked towards the gate, and then a group of men was taken away. That is those who were to be exchanged, and they would be escorted by those. Later on, I heard those were policemen from Trebinje but I learned that later when I was exchanged. And among the exchanged, (redacted) was one of them, and he told me all that happened to them as they were taking them to the place of exchange, how this group of soldiers ill-treated them, I mean this same group of soldiers who had come to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when this incident occurred? From where did you see it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Room 20, and we were lined up in the passage facing the front door, waiting for our turn to go to lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know -- can you name any of the victims of this incident? Do you recall who was beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once again, it was by mishap. Nihad Pasovic fared worst.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the only time that you saw such an occurrence, that soldiers or policemen from outside beat detainees in the yard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the only time that I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your previous statement that you gave to the Prosecutor's office, you described this incident, but you mentioned that it was in August 1992, and now you say it was in October 1992. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, it has to do with the place of exchange. Two groups were taken in August. One was taken to the area of Konjic and the other one to the area of Kalinovik. The group that I mentioned on the 31st of October, Konjic. And I must have -- not must have. I simply made a mistake with the date, with the group of the 31st of August and the 31st of October, which also went to be exchanged in Konjic. Now I'm positive and I'm sure it was on the 31st of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the incident is listed in the indictment under 5.8, but it seems to be a mistake. It seems to be that it's the same incident like 5.13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understand. You mean the description is of what happened in 5.13 --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Point 8. But the date, the date is wrong, obviously, and we have this incident twice in the indictment. That is, at least, what it looks like at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you arrived in the KP Dom, how many detainees were there already?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 570 detainees in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? It's a very precise number.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very precise and accurate, because as of the first day when I arrived in my dormitory, number 20, with an inmate, we counted every day how many men went to have breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and how many of them came back. We could not know if there were people in isolation cells and how many, but at that time that was the accurate number, 570 detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the KP Dom 29 months and 16 days, as you said, later, how many detainees were left at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sixty-one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left, did any Muslim detainees stay behind or were you the last group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were the last group, except that I and the first 50 were exchanged on the 6th of October; and there was a group of 10 -- that is, 11 men at Kula, and they were exchanged ten days later in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were detainees exchanged before that, and do you know if they all were actually exchanged?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. There were exchanges at various times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have already mentioned that some of these people - you have mentioned some by name - disappeared in such exchanges. What is your estimation how many people disappeared in exchanges all together?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 450 men disappeared through these exchanges. Four hundred fifty-seven, to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? How did you come to this precise figure?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I had and have a list of all those detained when I was there; not the names of all the exchanged, but I have the numbers and I have the number of the missing ones, bearing in mind the figure of 570 and it varied between that and 752, because some were taken away and some were brought in - it was like a shift - and according to some indicia, or rather according to what I was told by those who had arrived there before me, because a large number had been turned over in the KP Dom before me. Because it was set up on the 6th or 8th of April, 1992, and I was brought there on the 25th of May, so there was a month before that and there was plenty of time to have a considerable turnover of people in those rooms, so that I have a figure that there were -- that more than 1.000 men had been at some time or other in the KP Dom in Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we do not need to go into the details of exchanges, but I would like to know: From the 21 people you came together with to the KP Dom, how many disappeared in exchanges? Do you know? Could you say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you that of 21 of us, 4, maybe 5, were exchanged, and those others were never exchanged. If you want me, I can give you the names of those exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "exchanged," do you mean who were alive, who you met later, or what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite. Those who survived, those who were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, can we have the witness shown and put in front of him again the sheet P426.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yes, but before you give us the names of those who survived, could you please check in the list first. So if you find a name on the list, please do not tell us the name, but the number. Yes, please. Tell us who survived besides you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Person under 8, under 109. Person 162 was brought from the same area but was not in my group. Then Munib Karovic also survived, Nezir Krdzdic from Srebrenica. And there are no more survivors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that -- in the beginning you mentioned that you were arrested together with Mr. Kameric and Mr. Babic. What happened to them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kameric and Babic were taken for one of the exchanges. I don't know where and I don't know what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you contact the relatives or did the relatives of these two contact you, and what did they tell you or ask you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Abdulah Kameric, I spoke to his wife - she is in the same place where I live now - and she also confirmed to me that she absolutely had no information about him, just as I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have already described to us yesterday that you had to clean the room where beatings had occurred. Did you have to work in the KP Dom on other occasions as well?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start working, and what did you work?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I began working so as to -- well, in a way, to hide. I began in the farm, then in the bakery, the furniture factory, within the compound. Later on I looked after lawns, flower lanes, and went to fell wood in the forest, and suchlike.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to work permanently in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 I did not have to work all the time, but I'm telling you: That work that I did, they were concealing me from the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to this later. And in 1993, did you have to work the entire year 1993?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to work throughout 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had to work. Does that mean you were forced to work or did you volunteer?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Absolutely. I would have never volunteered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were hidden, hidden. Why hidden? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever the Red Cross came - and I never knew about them. I never knew they were coming - they would single out a group of 22 men, and it would all happen so quickly in the morning hours and they would take us to the bakery and we would spend the whole day in its cellar doing nothing, just staring at that dust and that product which comes out of the bakery. And that is how they would keep us the whole day until the evening, until somebody would tell them that the Red Cross, if it had come to visit, had completed the visit and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever talk with one of the prison staff about why you were always taken away when the Red Cross came?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I did not -- nobody would tell me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have a conversation with a person Gojko Jokanovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes we talked about family matters, family problems, about our relations, about medicines which I needed, and suchlike.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that a particular group of people were hidden from the Red Cross. Did these detainees in this group have anything in common, that made them particular?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think, if I -- I dare say it was prominent citizens of Foca. That was one common feature, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak with Gojko Jokanovic about your group being separated from others?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We asked him that. We did ask him. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know what is the purpose of this question. First the question was whether the witness talked with Gojko Jokanovic. The witness said he discussed family matters with Gojko Jokanovic and medicines, and then the third question again is whether with Gojko Jokanovic. That is, it is a leading question, trying to make the witness say something. The question was whether the witness talked with Gojko Jokanovic, and the witness said, "We talked about family matters and medicines." And then again there was a question whether he discussed a group of people with Gojko Jokanovic. This is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, it is not a leading question. It is an attempt to refresh his recollection, as I understand it. If there is something in the statement that he gave, then counsel could have simply shown him his statement and say, "Does that refresh your recollection about something else you said, too?" It's not a leading question. Certainly, the Prosecution or any counsel has to ensure that the witness has exhausted his recollection before seeking to refresh it. And if that is your objection, we might ask the Prosecution to proceed to do so. But it is not a leading question. A leading question is one which suggests the answer, and that one does not suggest the answer. It's purely refreshing his recollection. Seeing there has been an objection taken, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, it might be better if you sought to ensure that he can recall nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And if there is a statement with this in it, you can show it to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall -- did you have a conversation with Gojko Jokanovic in relation to your particular group of 22 people that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen, there were times when I talked to him and when we asked him whether he knew why we were separated. As far as I can remember, his answer was that we were being prepared for some kind of an exchange for big fish, as they called it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this conversation take place? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could go and see Gojko when I was sick, I guess. And that was not permitted, and that was not possible, actually, until after August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Let us now talk about the prison structure. Who was the warden before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, the warden of the prison, of the KP Dom, was Radojica Tesovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know him from before?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him, because he was my pedagogy teacher in school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who replaced him during your time of detention?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was replaced by Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Krnojelac from before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well did you know him? Can you tell us what your relation was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew him relatively well. We said hello to each other. We would meet each other in town and (redacted), et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Krnojelac involved in politics? In particular was he involved in the SDS politics?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only make assumptions. I'm not sure. I assume he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Did you ever see him with -- on SDS rallies?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not attend SDA -- SDS rallies, but I saw him in the company of persons who were in and around the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which persons did you see him with?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a few times I saw him in the company of teacher Kasalica; once or twice perhaps in the company of Matovic, Vujadin; Cicovic, Velko; Stankovic, he's a teacher too, Vojko, I think, yes; Jovo Stankovic, Zarko Vukovic. I don't know. Perhaps I could remember other names too but I have enumerated quite a few, haven't I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You said that you saw him in the company of SDS members or people around the SDS. Those you just told us, these teachers, were they SDS members? Do you mean these people?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Them specifically, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that they were SDS members or around the SDS, as you said?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veljko Cicovic I had the opportunity of seeing him in a group where SDS meetings were held, and also Vojko Stankovic. As for teacher Kasalica, he publicly stated that he was SDS and that was well known in town. Even the children whom he taught knew that as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Mr. Krnojelac in the company of these men, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they socialised. They usually went for a walk on the right bank of the Drina, from the municipality building, and then over the bridge. Sorry, the left bank, when you cross the bridge, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them attend rallies together, or political meetings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Krnojelac in the company of high-ranking SDS politicians?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had the opportunity of seeing him in 1991, 1992, the end, either just before the new year or after the new year, 1991, 1992. When I was leaving the Ribarski restaurant with my deputy director, I saw Mr. Krnojelac with Vojo Maksimovic, Velibor Ostojic, and there was another person whom I did not recognise. I guess he was the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw them? What were you doing at that moment?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had just finished this visit with my deputy director. We were walking downstairs and my deputy director said hello to Vojo Maksimovic and Velibor Ostojic. So did I. And then we each went our own way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they going, this group of people, including Mr. Krnojelac? Where were they going?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They entered the Ribarski restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them arrive together?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can assume that they did arrive together because they were very close to the car that was supposed to be taken back in order to be parked. This was just by the steps leading to the Ribarski restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Krnojelac have a function in the reserve army, do you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that he was a reserve captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw him earlier on in that uniform, and in 1990 I had one of my last exercises. As we were finishing up parts of this exercise, we were in the hotel, we were all having lunch together. Mr. Krnojelac came there together with Mr. Cancar -- I beg your pardon. At that time, that man was head of defence in Foca. Of course, everybody was eating, and he came with Luka, and he said, "I'm satisfied, everything is fine, and the commander is satisfied as well." And Mr. Krnojelac also nodded his head and said, "I am satisfied." At that time, I believed that he held the post of commander of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself, did you have a function in the reserve army?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the exercise that you just mentioned, you said in 1990. Can you be more specific when in 1990?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's September. It was a rainy day. I remember. (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you saw Mr. Krnojelac in the hotel. What hotel?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zelengora hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Krnojelac wearing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a military uniform, of course, with the insignia belonging to the rank that he had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned this other person who was with him.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luka Cancar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what position did he have? Was he the commander you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luka Cancar was the secretary of National Defence, as it was called in later times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A local secretary or from the higher level?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a person who doesn't wear a uniform. He was in charge of defence affairs in the town of Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that this person referred to the commander being satisfied. Who was the commander who was satisfied?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you approximately. I assumed that since Mr. Krnojelac said, "I am satisfied, thank you, thank you, I am satisfied," I assumed that he was commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Krnojelac in this kind of uniform on other occasions before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, when there were exercises and preparations. I also had to respond to such call-ups. I saw him in the premises of the National Defence secretariat. He wore the uniform and insignia of a captain. And I also had an address book of persons who held certain posts. However, I did not have the exact post of Mr. Krnojelac, whether he was commander of the Territorial Defence or whether he held a higher post than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "address book," what kind of address book do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: An address book of all the active persons in conditions of war and any other conditions that have to be called first and foremost and with whom contact had to be established. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted). That is the speciality I had, and that is what I trained for when I did my military service in Topcider, in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And until the beginning of the war, was Mr. Krnojelac still in this address book, or was he taken off, for whatever reason?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The address book that I had, if you want me to tell you, I'll tell you that I had this at home, because I was allowed to have it at home. I think that his name was never deleted from the list of responsible persons, military persons, who had to be called up in cases when there was an imminent danger of war, any kind of emergency, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Krnojelac in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he wearing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any rank insignia on this uniform?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not notice that because I really did not show any interest in it either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see him in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not very often, but when we went for breakfast, during those days when he just came in in June 1992, perhaps for about seven or ten days, and later they probably changed the premises where breakfast would be served. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak with Mr. Krnojelac while you were in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not speak with him, but I did meet him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you meet him, and where?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the month of July, in front of Room 11. I was working on park maintenance. Mr. Krnojelac came in with three or four men and he was escorted by a guard. They entered my building. While he was returning, I was so close to him that I said hello and I asked him for a cigarette, and he just waved me off and said, "Get lost."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see if he recognised you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what he'll say, how much he does know me or doesn't know me, but I believe that he did recognise me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What makes you believe that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because we were never in any close contact or did we have any close conversations. Whatever happened was basically that we would meet in the street and say hello to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said he was with three or four men. Who were they? How were they dressed and what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were persons who were dressed in military uniform, and later I found out, or rather the guard told me that this was a delegation that had come because the premises of the KP Dom were supposed to be renovated, so they were touring them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that it was in July. Which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- you mentioned when you saw Mr. Krnojelac. Did you see him during daytime and night-time or only during daytime?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day I saw him during daytime, and there were occasions when I could see him at the window in the late night hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where -- what window are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The window of his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was his office?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His office faced my building, in the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which floor was it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first floor, if I disregard the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you a photo. It's the Exhibit 18 photo, 7472. There is a part of the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We do not have -- not so focused, please.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is showing -- can we have the full photo so that I can count the windows? Yes. The witness is showing onto the second floor, not counting the -- counting the ground floor as the ground floor, is pointing at the second window from the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are you pointing at? What is it that you point out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And what is it? What are you showing us? The window, what is it? Can you point --

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What window are you pointing at? What room is it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now the witness is pointing on the first floor, one window below.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are you pointing at? What -- do you want to point out to us the room, Mr. Krnojelac's office, or what are you pointing at, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep confusing me. I'm trying to get my math right. First floor, second floor, and for you this is the second floor. And in your words, the office was on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. We are asking you. We are asking you. On which floor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's what we've been calling the second floor.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. It is this floor and that window.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is now pointing at the second floor, second window from the left. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I think in the transcript it would probably be better to also say that it was the window shown in the plan of the room where a number of other witnesses have identified as Mr. Krnojelac's office; otherwise, every time we have to pull the photograph out to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you saw him at the window. What was he doing when you saw him at the window?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion I saw him, the window was open. He was smoking by the window. He was walking by the window and smoking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Krnojelac at night-time at that window?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps twice or three times. He was not alone. One could always notice the presence of other persons as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Mr. Krnojelac, did he ever carry a weapon? Could you see it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the inner compound of the KP Dom mined?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was mined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see when it was mined?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the compound of the KP Dom was mined sometime in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did this? Who actually laid the mines?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A group for mining came, a group of soldiers, of course. I recognised Milun Milanovic, commander of that group; and Trojer Zelimir, a miner; and a miner, Sajin, nicknamed Saja. I knew his name too, but I can't remember it now. I recognised him as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Krnojelac present while this happened, while the mines were laid?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krnojelac did accompany that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him with this group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I personally saw him with that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he doing, if anything?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He talked. That I saw for sure. He was talking with Mr. Milun Milanovic. He was moving his hand. I don't know what these movements were related to, but you could see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was Mr. Krnojelac replaced?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was there about a year, so it was 1993, was it, until the 6th or 8th of June, 1993, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who replaced him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Sekulovic came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the conditions change after Mr. Krnojelac was replaced?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They absolutely did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the better or for the worse? In which way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the better. For the better. Although I had work duty, the food was of much better quantity and you could get more than you could during Mr. Krnojelac's time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, while you were detained in the KP Dom, did you see a person Savo Todovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw an individual called Savo Todovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him from before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness come closer to the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, would you move up closer to the microphone. They are having difficulty hearing you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what he did before the war, what work he did?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, he worked as a guard for a while. After that, I know he was a civil servant in charge of labour affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were detained in the KP Dom, what was his function?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mention two functions that I know he discharged: In charge of labour affairs and deputy warden in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that he was in charge of labour affairs? Did you have dealings with him while you worked in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did, true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that he was the deputy warden?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply heard it from guards who guarded us, and people who learned about it in a direct contact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him in the prison, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how often did you see him in the prison?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him very often; not every day perhaps but very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he treat the detainees? And in particular, how did he treat you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me begin with how he treated me. A list would come to the dormitory, a list of persons to go to work, and I was one of them. And after enter -- when I would enter the interior of the building, I would meet him, and he'd give the guards a list of people, and the work assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever mistreat you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not beat me. He did abuse me verbally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once, when I failed to turn up at the -- in the mine for work, the next morning, when I was called out again to go to work, and I was really ill, and I risked it, I risked not to go to work, a guard came to fetch me and said, "Savo wants to see you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And did you see Savo, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to complain to him, to tell him that I was ill and so on and so forth, and he said, "This is not your former time nor your former workplace, to do what -- as you please. You're going to work, period."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that that you had this conversation?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conversation was in 1993, about the time when I started working in the mine. So it was October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you risked not to go to work. Why was it a risk?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a risk because afterward, he could take -- they could take me to the isolation cell and beat me as likely as not, as it happened to other people, and I suppose there is something even worse after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall to which people that actually happened? Do you recall anyone?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first if somebody gave up or could not go to work for a reason, then he had to go to a doctor, if there was a doctor, or rather, the medical technician, Gojko Jokanovic. And going to a doctor, that is, a nurse, he would then control why did the one who did not want or could not go to work go to see the doctor [as interpreted]. And I know how Dedovic -- and I remember his first name too. I know he was a house Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. painter. He refused that on a couple of times and he was taken away and beaten in the isolation cell. Yes, Fehim Dedovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Rasevic already. What position did he have, Mitar Rasevic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitar Rasevic was guard commander in the camp security, or, to put it simply, commander, as they called him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in the prison on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes, I did, quite often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he wear when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a military uniform too, although at times he would change it and put on the former uniform of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he treat the detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you specifically, and I will begin with myself. I had some contact with him, but not contact of a kind that he would persecute me. I was not persecuted by him, and I do not know that he persecuted others. I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "persecuted"?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he persecuted, whether he was after other people, whether he was the one who assigned or tortured or beat people, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him for help and did he help you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did ask for help when I needed medicines when I contracted pneumonia, and he answered, "You know well where you are. You know what times are these and that medicines cannot be provided."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guards, were they the former prison guards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those whom I knew, and other people who knew them, yes, absolutely, all the former guards of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they wear? What kind of clothing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them wore military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout your detention or did this vary?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them would change into the old KP Dom uniform, but not all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave the KP Dom? On what day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 4th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was present when you left the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitar Rasevic was present, and a group of guards who searched our affairs, our belongings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they searching for?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we were told what we should not take out of the KP Dom, if we had any books, if we had appropriated, taken something from the KP Dom, and at times we made some ornamental boxes or cigarette holders, and they would seize it all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said when you left the KP Dom there were 61 people. Were they all together with you? Did they all leave together with you the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they left with me, all of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us to a place called Kula, near Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the camp staff accompany you on the bus -- on the vehicle you went?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mitar Rasevic came along and a policeman from the town police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how -- in which vehicle were you taken to Kula?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The driver, what was he wearing? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it very well. He had a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you actually exchanged on that 4th of October?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were not exchanged on that 4th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived, on the right, to the right, there was a police outpost at Kula, and that was the first time for me to visit the area. On the left-hand side were the premises where detainees were kept. And our bus was to enter the yard of those premises, presumably to put us into one of those rooms. However, no sooner did we stop on a platform in front of those rooms, a police car arrived -- than the police car arrived with three armed soldiers and threatened the driver and ordered, "Turn back. Who ordered to do this without me?" And that is the real voice and his real words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that person who ordered --

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not recognise him because he had a long beard, a beret, and at that moment, I could not recognise him. So the bus turned round and he sat in the police car with a driver and that other individual, and went in front of the bus and took us back in the direction of Foca, to a place called Miljevina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mitar Rasevic do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitar Rasevic was in the police administration. He had stayed behind, presumably to negotiate our further fate or the exchange, and they would not allow him to return on the bus. He just stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said they would not allow him. Who would not allow him to enter -- re-enter the bus?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group that was in the police car. Three men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us in the direction, Trnovo, Rogoj, Dobro Polje, Miljevina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this matter actually resolved?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And after a long wait, sometime around 7.00 or 8.00 in the evening, it lasted until then, and the new warden of the KP Dom from Foca, Zoran Sekulovic, came with a driver, and with the command of that locality, because Miljevina is not much a town so I call it a locality. So with the command of that locality, he conducted negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you returned on the same day to Kula, after these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were taken back to Kula, around 8.00 in the evening. We left Miljevina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you released or exchanged? On which day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of October, between half past 7.00 and 8.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your time of detention in the KP Dom, we have already discussed the physical consequences of this. Did your detention affect your psychological health?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, very much so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because when I arrived to a place where I live in, I had to undergo psychiatric treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What effects, what mental effects, did you notice on you? Why did you go to a psychiatrist?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not feel up to making independent movements. At times my thinking capacity was at a level of a child. I needed somebody to escort me, to accompany me into the street. I could not move about independently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you -- were you treated for this mental condition?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from, I should say, beginning of 1995 until the summer of 1996, I was under constant supervision, and even now I often have to ask for a psychiatrist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you still now need counselling? What affects you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frequent headaches and this lack of stability, that never stops. Even now I have a problem. I cannot stand for more than 15 minutes or to walk for one hour. It is simply too difficult for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are the questions of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Bakrac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Mihajlo Bakrac and I am one of the counsel for the accused Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you something. It was much easier during the examination in chief because my learned friend speaks a different language so there was a time between the question and answer. But you and I speak the same language and this could cause some problems. So will you please, when you hear my question, wait a while for it to be interpreted, and then to answer, to make the work of interpreters easier and to make it easier for the Chamber to follow the cross-examination? So, sir, are you still the president of the club of detainees of the KP Dom in that place, in a state where you live in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you become the president of the detainees association?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And between August, 1995 -- or when did you communicate -- did you have contact with the detainees from the KP Dom before that date?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have contact with KP Dom detainees and discuss the KP Dom and conditions there before you gave a statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you quite sure? Did you, in your statement to the OTP, you say that you communicated with people and discussed with them the conditions in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when I gave my statement, I did not have an opportunity to talk to -- to talk with detainees because I did not know where -- I did not know their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I will read to you an excerpt from your statement which you gave to the Prosecution, that is to the investigators of the OTP, on the 20th of May, 1996: "I maintain contact with other detainees of the KP Dom. We meet from time to time to refresh our memories." Is it true? Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true, but I think the year is not correct, because in 1995 -- I think it was 1995 that I gave my first statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you then give them yet another statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be sure about the time frame. And what I said in that statement, it was all based on my recollection, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, but I'm asking you: Did you give another statement or not, in 1996? Did you give a statement to the OTP in 1996? The date does not matter.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did give a statement in 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you said what I have just read to you, that you were meeting other detainees from the KP Dom and that you were talking with them? Is it true or is it not true?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
