utterances.text: Sir, you are trying to link this situation with the whole situation of people who were taken out. I covered my ears at the time when the second group was taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you linked all those situations even if you did not hear that situation?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw people being taken out and I knew what had happened to those Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. first group, and I absolutely lacked the courage to listen to that again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the first group, you did not hear anything, it is merely your assumption that the same thing happened as with the first group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In your earlier statements to the OTP and in the public security centre, did you ever mention in any one of them that the second, the third, and the fourth group were taken out to the central part of the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you then mention it now for the first time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because earlier I stated that I listened to the torture and the beating of the first two groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm not sure if anyone asked me about the second one, that is whether I was asked where they had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand you well, just a while ago you said that as of the second group, you stopped listening?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are making horrible mistakes, really. I did not listen to the beating of the second group and I did listen to those others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. You also mentioned that you had heard a voice asking Nurko Nisic, "Nurko, where's your flag?" And you also said that before he was taken out, Nurko had told you that his flag had been found, that -- so then why should somebody ask him about his flag if it had been found in his desk and seized?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The flag was allegedly found, and Nurko said that he did indeed have a Croatian flag and the one who asked him that and what he -- and why he asked him that, that is none of my business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said, sir, that -- or rather my question is: After which group did you clean the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of all the beatings -- groups, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also clean the rooms in the right wing of the administrative building, looking from your room, or in the centre part of the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the central part, I did not clean any rooms. I cleaned the rooms in the right wing of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you agree, and according to what you said, the first group was taken out on the 12th of June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not say that it was the 12th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so when was the first group taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 12th and some June, three or four days after the 12th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the last group taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last group was -- could have been taken out around the 25th or 6th, 23rd or 24th. Does not matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you told us it went on until the 28th, so it lasted until the 23rd or 4th, not the 28th.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It went on until the 28th. And I have the reserve information that it wasn't on the 12th of June precisely, nor that the last day was precisely the 28th. It was between those two dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if we accept what you are telling us now, which is different from what you told us before, you said the 12th and then two or three days later, and then you said the 25th, which is two or three days less, so there is a difference of ten days. So they took to you clean those rooms ten days later after what had happened.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you are not judging this correctly. I told -- I already said that I cleaned those rooms in August. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was two months after all this had happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you find in those rooms?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found a couple of wooden handles and a metal rod.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And naturally, I also spotted blood stains, dried blood stains.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the rooms that you cleaned? On the photograph you showed it behind a metal door, behind a metal bars. You pointed at the first room on the right. How large was it and what was there in it? Did you clean it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did clean it. It's not a large room. I cannot be very accurate about its size. It could have been 3 by 2.5 or 3. It doesn't matter. I don't know the dimensions. I never measured it. And I already told you what I had found there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what else was there in that room? I mean furniture, was there any furniture?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was completely bare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you clean the room next to it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cleaned it and sat in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how large is that room and what was in it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a smaller room and there was a desk and a chair -- there were a desk and a chair in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say smaller, of a smaller -- how much -- how big was it, roughly?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 2.5 to 3 metres, roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you clean the third room again next to that one?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think I moved on to clean the passage and another person cleaned those rooms; that is, that third room towards the staircase to the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the room that you cleaned and which you first mentioned that the first one to the right from the metal door, was that the first room, the next room to the staircase leading to the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not next to the staircase but next to the reception room, the first room after the metal door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in front of that door and that room, is there a staircase leading to the upper floor of the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staircase is on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I have to look for a photograph. Could the usher help me, please, to show the witness photograph 8448? Could I have it on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now, if I understood what you said the metal door with the metal bars are marked in yellow as 1, and it -- that is the room that you cleaned first, that you pointed at?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is indicating the first room on the right-hand side behind the metal door marked with 1, marked 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the door marked 2, where does this door lead to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this door but I think that it was the switchboard, the telephone exchange behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And door number 3, do you know where that door leads to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the witness spoke about the door of the telephone exchange, the witness indicated the door marked on the photograph with 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of the door marked 2, and you cannot see this on the photograph, but do you recall was there any other room here or not?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There shouldn't be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a staircase in front of the door leading to an upper floor or is it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a staircase on the left-hand side, next to the receptionist's; rather, three or four stairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show to us on this photograph on which side do you say the staircase leading to the upper floor of the administrative building is?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the upper floor of the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind this metal door, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is the staircase which leads to the upper floor of the administrative building, did it face the yard of the KP Dom or did it face the street in front of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you enter to the left, you take the stairs to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. What I'm asking you is: If the passage is in the middle, is the staircase on the side of the building nearer the prisoners' quarters and the KP Dom yard, the KP Dom compound, or is the staircase on the side nearer the street?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staircase is nearer the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, when you were talking about the beatings that you suffered in the KP Dom, in your first statement for the Office of the Prosecutor you mentioned that you were mistreated twice. In your second statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1996, you said you were physically mistreated three times. Yesterday and today, during your examination-in-chief, you said that you were physically abused four times. Please be kind enough and tell us which is correct.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most correct version is that I was mistreated four times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell the Prosecutor that in your first statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The period in July when I was abused, I didn't have any major injuries or consequences, so I simply forgot about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you thought that the fact you were beaten up was unimportant and you didn't have to tell the Prosecutor about it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't beaten up seriously, and I didn't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't remember the date, but you must have remembered that you were beaten.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remembered that I was beaten, and I repeatedly said it was two or three times. Later on, when I concentrated and looked back closer, I remembered it was four times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said today that you were beaten when you made gloves and socks out of blankets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1996, you said the following: "All the time the prisoners were punished and put in isolation cells for even minor offences. For instance, when Safet Avdic, Rasim Hanjalic, Ibrahim Kafedzic made socks out of blankets, they were punished." You described a specific incident and you didn't say at all that you too made socks and that you were punished and beaten up because of it.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't make socks, but socks were found on me, one in my hand and another set on my feet. But the mentioned prisoners made the socks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is another detail that you've only just remembered?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't remember it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you didn't tell the Office of the Prosecutor about such Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. an important incident?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't remember this detail for a long time, that is, why I was put in solitary confinement and mistreated. Then I linked up the situation with the bread and then I remembered that it was because of the socks that I was put in solitary confinement and mistreated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in the KP Dom, did you have any facilities for hygiene?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first year, no. We would sometimes be given a cake of soap to wash our clothes, but in cold water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1995, on page 5, you said: "We were enabled to keep clean"?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That came later, when that year expired, that is, at the end of 1992 or in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you say that to the Prosecutor? The way you spoke, it appeared that throughout the period you did have the necessary sanitary conditions.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have refreshed my memory now. I remember things much better now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, sir, whether the guards, during your two-year detention, went to the front lines?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did, because there were quite lengthy periods when we were guarded and secured by a couple of people who did not change for up to seven days, the same people for up to seven days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever, earlier on, tell the Office of the Prosecutor about the incident with a person surnamed Pasovic, also known as Pace, in the yard of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did describe that event once. Now I'm not sure whether I mentioned his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remembered his name now?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you say "now." I didn't come here with information that I recalled just before coming here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the incident with Pasovic, known as Paco, was not mentioned in any of your statements to the Office of the Prosecutor or the security centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but my recollection came later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with this incident, you said that you were lined up in front of the door to Room 20. Do you mean inside that room or outside, in front of the room, in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The inside of that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the central part?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In front of that central room, the corridor leading to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that corridor have windows?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, quite big windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, I should like to go back to the statement that we received in the meantime. So with the assistance of the usher, I should like the witness to mark his signature on the document, which is now complete and has all three pages to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is this a completely fresh copy of it, is it, so you want him to start again?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It is the copy that we were given by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you be kind enough, wherever you see your signature on this statement, to mark it with a sign. You can mark it with a letter "X" if you like, next to your signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, for your information, the document that we have in the evidence vault is a copy that we received from the Bosnian government. We do not have an original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: My concern was only about marking an original document, that's all. That's why I asked. Now, should that document be replaced in our binders? Are there copies for us?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll deal with that later. Thank you. What is its ID number? You did give it to us earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Bakrac, is there any real issue now as to whether that is his signature? It's the same signature on each page at the foot of the page, complying with what you say is in your criminal procedure act.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. My question is for the witness to tell us whether all three pages contain his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. If, of course, you are seeking to use this in some way, as you appear to be, threatening to launch some sort of prosecution against him, he would have to be warned that he does not have to answer the question. That's why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, I will do that. You are under oath, sir, and you're obliged to look carefully to see whether that is your signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't think you got the point that I was seeking to make. It may be that I misunderstood what you said, but when you warned him about the provisions of the statute, if you are seeking to use or you are going to seek to use his answer to that question in some way as the basis for some form of prosecution of him, he should be warned that he does not have to answer that question because he's not obliged to incriminate himself, just as your client was given that warning on every occasion he was asked to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there's a misunderstanding. I was asked by the witness. I said that according to the law on criminal procedure of the country where the statement was taken, every page has to be signed at the bottom. It wasn't any threat of prosecution. I just answered a question put to me by the witness, which I wasn't obliged to do. When he said that there was a signature on the first page, I said that according to the law on criminal procedure, the document has to be signed on every page, at the bottom of every page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is all that noise that's going on outside something to do with the security problem? Could anybody hear that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, as long as our happy security service is not having another rehearsal for clearing out the building in the middle of a trial, we'll proceed until we hear to the contrary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think my signature on page 3 is questionable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean that it is not your signature or that it is or that you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It must have been copied. Your Honour, may I address the court? Regarding the first two signatures, I can confirm that they are mine. As for the third, I shall try to establish the truth in the service in which I gave that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, sir, thank you very much for that. Bearing in mind they are photostats, there is always some difficulty in determining whether or not the signature is the same, but if Mr. Bakrac wants to proceed to have that checked, he can do so, as he did, in fact, threaten earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I have already said that there was a misunderstanding. I just explained why there is a signature on every page, according to the rules, and I told the witness that his signature could be subject to handwriting expert opinion, but I think any further comments would be superfluous. The Defence feels that what we heard from the witness regarding these statements suffices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, as my final question, I would like to ask the witness whether now, while looking at his signatures, he also read the statement.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't read it through. The first part does coincide with what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me now whether this statement is fully -- is entirely incorrect, partly incorrect, whether you did say everything that is written in it to the investigator, which part of it was erroneously recorded? So will you tell us whether you made this statement or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think before the witness can actually answer this question, he needs time to read it. Otherwise, how would he then answer this question now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that's fair enough. He did say he hadn't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did ask him, and he said he had read it partially, but not to be at fault for using too much time, I was trying to speed things up. But, of course, let the witness read it through.

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I address you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Speed sometimes is dangerous, Mr. Bakrac. Yes, sir, what do you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know, Your Honour, but you cautioned me once that I shouldn't be too cautious, so I'm in a dilemma now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, sir what is it that you wanted to ask?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a part of the statement - and you've already asked me about that, sir - regarding Ramo Dzendusic, Adil Seco [phoen], Fadil Sevko [phoen], somebody I don't know, I am certain, and I can guarantee 100 per cent, that at least as far as Adil and Ramo, I could say every -- whenever I was asked what happened to them, and what is written in this statement is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, will you agree with me that in this statement, it says that they were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will not agree, because they disappeared and they were never exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, as you have read the statement: Will you agree with me that this statement says that they were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have we got the original? I'm sorry, not the original, the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's in the trial binder and it's 135A, and the passage talked about is on the third page in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And which binder is 135? You will see what I mean about how difficult it is to find documents in these problems. I have now found it. Page 3, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, first paragraph, the top paragraph, the last two sentences of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I wouldn't like this to depend upon the accuracy of the translation. Have you seen this translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And it says there, "The following men were taken to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. be exchanged." Now, if you are suggesting there is some distinction between that and "they were exchanged", it may be that the original is ambiguous. There is a difference, I understand, between actually being exchanged and being taken to be exchanged, but if there is one thing we have learned during the course of this trial, the fact that people were told they were being exchanged often meant they would disappear. And that's all that the witness has said here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is not the point, with all due respect. I do apologise, but Dzendusic, Ramo, in the examination-in-chief, and also in his statement, was described as a person who was taken out as a member of a group that was beaten up in the KP Dom and ended up in the way we were told. That is the point, because the witness in his first statement says that this person was taken to be exchanged, and here, in his testimony, he speaks about him as a person who was one of the victims in the KP Dom, so two different accounts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. I see now. You're suggesting that his evidence was that he disappeared after being beaten up, and here he is saying simply that they were not seen again after having being taken to be exchanged. Can you put it to him in those terms rather than us poring through documents? It's a valid issue for you to raise, but put it to him directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have asked the question about Ramo Dzendusic and then showed him the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness, is Ramo Dzendusic the person who was among one of the groups that were beaten up and killed in the KP Dom, as you said, or a person who was taken away allegedly to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramo Dzendusic was in the fourth group of persons who were beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that it says in this statement that he was taken allegedly to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence suggests the admission of this statement into evidence, and we have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. What do you say about the admission of the document, the statement into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the B/C/S original will be Exhibit D-2, and the English translation will be Exhibit D-2A. Have you finished the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I thought I had already said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I had not intended in any way a criticism in the way I asked that. I just wanted to know. Is there any re-examination, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just a very few matters. Re-examined by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned when asked by Defence counsel that Gojko Jankovic said that nothing can happen to the prisoners without the order of the military command. Did you hear him say that personally or did he say that to someone else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gojko Jankovic said that first to the men who were working for him in renovating his cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this person renovate the cafe? Was it a detainee or who was the person who did that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Fehim Dedovic, and Hajric -- I know his nickname but I can't remember his first name. A cafe was renovated of the former JNA club. He probably took it over as his possession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you get this information that Gojko Jankovic said that to these two gentlemen? How did you learn about it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They passed it on to us when they came back from town. They told us about it, because they worked for him for about a month and longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally speak with Gojko Jankovic about this issue?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Defence counsel referred to this incident with Pace, and actually as you have told us during the examination in chief, there were two incidents involving this Pace. And you described to us that Pace was once beaten by Predrag Stefanovic and where were you when he was beaten as -- when he was beaten alone?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was lined up in front of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second time, is that when you were lined up in Room 20?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one more matter that I would like to clarify with you. You said that you saw and heard what happened to the first group, and you said when the second group was taken out and taken into the building, you covered your ears. Does that mean you didn't hear anything at all?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You can't put it that way, that I didn't hear anything at all. Occasionally, I would remove my hands. So you can't say that I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the second group was beaten in the same place as the first group. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-71 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because other people were watching also. They had the courage to peep through the window and see what was happening across the way from us.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I should have added that that exhibit, D-2 and D-2A are both under seal. Thank you, sir, for giving your evidence. You are now free to leave. I suggest you wait there for a moment because the blinds will have to be brought down to enable to you leave the court without being seen by the public. We will adjourn now until 9.30 in the morning.
